results.summary: This project implements an 8-bit pseudo-random number generator based on a 16-bit linear feedback shift register with a twist: the upper and lower halves are rotated in opposite directions and XORed. It is tested by observing the generated sequence on the output pins, and the initialization seed can be changed via the input pins. All-zero initialization is invalid and produces a constant zero output. The design is notable for its modified LFSR structure that combines two rotated halves.

This project generates an I2S bit clock by counting system clock cycles and producing a divided clock signal. It is used with an I2S audio interface, and the clock frequency is determined by the count value. The design includes a counter and a clock divider. It is notable for its role in audio clock generation.

This project implements a first-order passive sigma-delta analog-to-digital converter that requires external resistors and a capacitor connected to a digital input pin. The analog input is sampled and converted to a digital output using sigma-delta modulation. It is tested by applying an analog voltage and observing the digital output. The design is notable for its use of passive components and sigma-delta technique.

This project is a placeholder submission that appears to involve a memristor-based multiplexer or accelerator. The documentation is sparse, and the design is incomplete. It is not clear how it is used or tested. The project is notable only for its mention of memristor technology.

This project is a RISC-V based system-on-chip that includes a CPU, memory, and UART, SPI, and QSPI interfaces. It is used by loading and running programs via the serial interfaces. The design includes a memory subsystem and peripheral interfaces. It is notable for its integration of a RISC-V core with multiple communication interfaces.

This project is a stepper motor controller that uses a SPI interface to receive commands. It generates stepper motor control signals and includes a timer and signal generator. It is tested by connecting stepper motors and observing the motor movement. The design is notable for its motor control capability.

This project is an audio synthesizer that generates sound using an LFSR-based noise source and an I2S output. It is controlled via SPI and includes a TRNG for randomness. The design produces audio output through an I2S interface. It is notable for its combination of synthesis and random generation.

This project is a clock domain crossing FIFO that handles data transfer between two asynchronous clock domains. It includes asynchronous FIFO logic and memory. It is used to safely pass data between different clock domains. The design is notable for its clock domain crossing implementation.

This project decodes a 4-bit binary input into a hexadecimal digit and displays it on a 7-segment display. The input is set via DIP switches, and the output is shown on the display. It is used for educational purposes to demonstrate binary-to-hex conversion. The design is notable for its simple decoder and display interface.

This project is a WS2812 LED controller that uses an I2C interface to receive commands and drives WS2812B LEDs. It includes a register file for storing LED data. It is tested by connecting WS2812B LEDs and an I2C master such as a microcontroller. The design is notable for its LED control capability.
